newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks drift lower in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks drift lower in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kongs stocks opened weaker on Monday morning on robust turnover, due chiefly to an active shift of funds out of blue chips and into China plays, brokers said.
"There is a weak undertone to the blue-chip sector, but red chips are still active," said Lino Delgado, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was trading 67 points lower at 12,578, with turnover was a heavy HK$2.26 billion after the first 30 minutes of trade.
China plays dominated the most active list.
"There are worries that the (U.S.) economic indicators due out this week will show more upward movement, that inflationary pressures are beginning to be a problem," Delgado added.
On Tuesday, the U.S. Employment Cost Index (ECI) for the first quarter of 1997 will be released and was likely to have a big impact on markets, Delgado said.
This report will be followed by the first quarter GDP data report on Wednesday and April employment data on Friday.
"It is difficult to see what will happen to red chips," Delgado said.

H-share China Eastern Airlines was the most actively traded red chip, rising HK$0.125 to HK$2.700 on very active trade of HK$283.10 million. The share is due to release its earnings for 1996 later on Monday.
Salomon Brothers recently raised its expectations for the company's 1996 earnings to 565 million yuan, a 12 percent increase over 1995.
Premier red chip CITIC Pacific gained HK$1.20 to HK$42.80 on turnover of HK$172 million.
China Merchants Hai Hong eased HK$0.10 to HK$8.45. The share rose about 41 percent last week.

The blue-chip commercial and industrial sector outperformed the rest of the market, lifted chiefly by CITIC Pacific and a continued positive response to the property development outlook of Swire Pacific, which added HK$0.25 to HK$59.25.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings lost HK$1.00 to HK$188.50.
The April Hang Seng Index futures contract was trading 30 points lower at 12,615. The contract expires on Tuesday.
